review_conclusions: Positional fixed and variable little-endian encodings preserve their historical wire options. Full slice decode rejects trailing bytes; prefix decode returns its consumed count, and stream decode leaves EOF validation to the caller.
The bounded stream/slice adapters cap successful byte consumption and decoder allocation claims separately; the shared 2GiB hard claim ceiling is not a serialized payload byte limit.
Container byte claims are checked against remaining wire input before payload allocation/read; peek does not advance consumed bytes, while successful reads and consume operations do.
Direct typed decoding validates all flattened nodes, root cardinality, container lengths, depth, duplicate object keys, finite numbers and strings before constructing a DeserializeOwned target.
Sequence/map visitors enforce remaining immediate elements and alternating key/value state; ignored values skip their complete subtree without materializing JSON.

String enum representation is reserved for unit variants, while one-entry objects carry variant payloads. Map key adapters parse numeric/finite/one-scalar character keys and retain owned target lifetimes.

Artifact cache callers explicitly check post-decode EOF, expected raw bytes and complete chunks. Navigation re-decodes the selected schema after reading its version prefix; animation stream decoding advances by the returned header offset.
All seven positional fixtures and reused binary/direct structural assertions were read; actual exact-source predicates were evaluated without executing Rust tests.
